parts.name: barrel shell

physics.Basic_description: Olive green anodized aluminum cylindrical tube forming the main body and battery compartment.
physics.Functional_description: Houses the batteries and electronics while providing a structural grip for the user.
physics.Grasped_description: The primary grasp target; a parallel jaw gripper should clamp around the mid-section of the cylinder.
physics.reason: Flashlight bodies are thin-walled tubes to minimize weight while enclosing batteries.

parts.description: Olive green anodized aluminum cylindrical tube forming the main body and battery compartment.
parts.function: Houses the batteries and electronics while providing a structural grip for the user.

parts.name: shoulder shell

physics.Basic_description: Olive green tapered metal section connecting the narrow barrel to the wider head.
physics.Functional_description: Structural transition zone that flares out to support the larger reflector assembly.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped if the barrel is occluded, though the taper may cause slippage without force closure.
physics.reason: Continuous with the barrel shell, enclosing the internal driver circuitry.

parts.description: Olive green tapered metal section connecting the narrow barrel to the wider head.
parts.function: Structural transition zone that flares out to support the larger reflector assembly.

parts.name: tail cap

physics.Basic_description: Black anodized metal cap at the rear end of the flashlight.
physics.Functional_description: Seals the battery compartment and typically houses the tail switch button.
physics.Grasped_description: Graspable at the very end, but small surface area makes it less stable than the barrel.
physics.reason: Screw-on caps are cup-shaped shells enclosing the spring contact and switch mechanism.

parts.description: Black anodized metal cap at the rear end of the flashlight.
parts.function: Seals the battery compartment and typically houses the tail switch button.

parts.name: clip mount

physics.Basic_description: Small yellow-highlighted ring or attachment point on the barrel for the pocket clip.
physics.Functional_description: Secures the pocket clip to the flashlight body.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flush to be a primary grasp point; avoiding it prevents damage.
physics.reason: Likely a solid retaining ring or integrated machined feature.

parts.description: Small yellow-highlighted ring or attachment point on the barrel for the pocket clip.
parts.function: Secures the pocket clip to the flashlight body.

parts.name: pocket clip

physics.Basic_description: Thin black metal strip attached to the side of the barrel.
physics.Functional_description: Allows the flashlight to be clipped onto a pocket or belt.
physics.Grasped_description: Flexible and thin; grasping here would likely bend the clip or fail to secure the object.
physics.reason: Stamped metal sheet, effectively solid for mass calculation purposes.

parts.description: Thin black metal strip attached to the side of the barrel.
parts.function: Allows the flashlight to be clipped onto a pocket or belt.

parts.name: head shell

physics.Basic_description: Olive green wide cylindrical housing at the front containing the light source.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the reflector and LED while acting as a heat sink.
physics.Grasped_description: A stable secondary grasp point due to its larger diameter and rigidity.
physics.reason: Encloses the reflector and optics; walls are thicker here for heat dissipation.

parts.description: Olive green wide cylindrical housing at the front containing the light source.
parts.function: Protects the reflector and LED while acting as a heat sink.

parts.name: reflector

physics.Basic_description: Shiny metallic conical surface inside the head, visible through the lens.
physics.Functional_description: Shapes and directs the light beam from the LED.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal component, not accessible for grasping without disassembly.
physics.reason: Reflectors are thin spun or stamped metal cones.

parts.description: Shiny metallic conical surface inside the head, visible through the lens.

parts.name: led emitter

physics.Basic_description: Tiny central component at the base of the reflector.
physics.Grasped_description: Microscopic relative to the object; impossible to grasp directly.
physics.reason: Solid state semiconductor package mounted on a PCB.

parts.description: Tiny central component at the base of the reflector.

parts.name: lens disc

physics.Basic_description: Transparent flat circular pane covering the front opening.
physics.Functional_description: Protects the internal optics from dust and water while allowing light transmission.
physics.Grasped_description: Slippery and fragile; grasping here risks breaking the glass or dropping the object.
physics.reason: Solid pane of glass, typically 2-4mm thick.

parts.description: Transparent flat circular pane covering the front opening.

parts.name: front bezel ring

physics.Basic_description: Olive green ring at the very front edge holding the lens and bezel teeth.
physics.Functional_description: Secures the lens assembly and provides a mounting point for the strike bezel.
physics.Grasped_description: Graspable near the front, but the teeth might interfere with soft grippers.
physics.reason: Ring structure screwing onto the head shell.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
